guide.summary: Own app, no certification (self-serve, wait none); Own app with certified listing (app review, wait about 10 business days).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Own app, no certification (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Own app with certified listing (app review, wait about 10 business days).

composio.note: Composio manages the OAuth app for the TODOIST toolkit. The separate TODOIST_MCP toolkit needs your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio's managed app works. For production you should use your own app so users see your app name instead of Composio, and to get dedicated quota.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across all Composio users
Enterprise customers who require your branding end-to-end
The separate Todoist MCP toolkit requires your own OAuth app

scenarios.label: Own app, no certification
scenarios.when_this_applies: You create your own Todoist app and let any user authorize it, without listing it in Todoist's integrations pages.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: Docs describe no review step for sharing the integration with users (c3, c4).

scenarios.approval: No provider review is described for sharing; certification is optional.

scenarios.label: Own app with certified listing
scenarios.when_this_applies: You also want a dedicated page on Todoist's Integrations Pages for more visibility.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count (form, icon, screenshots, demo video), not measured

waiting.basis: c9: Todoist aims to respond within ten business days.

scenarios.approval: Optional certification with submission, technical and marketing review.
extras: Todoist not primary name; add non-affiliation statement.

modifiers.note: Todoist not primary name; add non-affiliation statement.

prerequisites.title: Todoist account
prerequisites.detail: Use is free with any Todoist account; some features depend on plan. If you need a Pro account for development, Todoist may help.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URIs must be configured in the App Management Console. For dynamically registered clients they must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

prerequisites.title: Marketing assets for certification
prerequisites.detail: Prepare a description, install instructions, website and privacy policy links, a 250x250 JPG icon, 1600x1000 JPG screenshots and a demo video, all in English.

steps.title: Create app in App Management Console
steps.detail: Log in, create the application and add your redirect URL. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config for the todoist toolkit through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes and test the flow
steps.detail: Pick the narrowest scopes, such as data:read_write, and connect a test account.
steps.done_when: A test user completes OAuth and a call succeeds.

steps.title: Draft certification materials
steps.detail: Write the description with the non-affiliation statement, the install instructions and the demo script.

steps.title: Record demo and submit form
steps.detail: Record the demo video, add the icon and screenshots, and submit the form.

steps.title: Wait for Todoist review
steps.detail: Todoist aims to respond within ten business days and replies to emails within two.

traps.title: Clients registered through dynamic registration do not have expiring
traps.detail: Clients registered through dynamic registration do not have expiring client secrets.

traps.title: Token limit blocks the app
traps.detail: Users are redirected with invalid_application_status when the app exceeds the maximum token limit or is suspended for abuse. The limit's value was not found.

traps.title: Naming and affiliation rules
traps.detail: Todoist cannot be the primary name; the description must say it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

traps.title: Meeting criteria is no guarantee
traps.detail: The certification criteria are representative only and do not guarantee approval. The app must not replicate Todoist features or rely solely on Zapier or IFTTT.

traps.title: Redirect URI mismatch
traps.detail: An unconfigured redirect URI returns a JSON error. With multiple URIs configured, redirect_uri is required.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded the maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Todoist to ask about the limit and your app's status.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the message to Todoist support.

blockers.what_it_means: redirect_uri was omitted although multiple redirect URIs are configured.
blockers.what_to_do: Send redirect_uri explicitly, matching a configured one.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the redirect URI in the request against the configured list.

open_questions: What is the maximum token limit per app? Ask Todoist developer support.
Is the certification review time longer than ten business days in practice? Ask Todoist or check recent submissions.
Does any provider review apply to apps shared widely without certification? Docs mention none; confirm with Todoist support.

evidence.quote: To authenticate other users, your application will need to obtain a token from them using the OAuth protocol.
evidence.answer: To authenticate other users, the app obtains a token from them via OAuth; the page describes this flow and mentions no provider review step for other users.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
evidence.answer: The task:add scope grants permission to add new tasks only; the app cannot read or modify existing data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
evidence.answer: The data:read scope grants read-only access to tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
evidence.answer: The data:read_write scope grants read and write access to tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
evidence.answer: The data:read_write scope includes the task:add and data:read scopes.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.
evidence.answer: The data:delete scope grants permission to delete tasks, labels, and filters.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants permission to delete projects.
evidence.answer: The project:delete scope grants permission to delete projects.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Grants permission to list backups with GET /api/v1/backups without MFA.
evidence.answer: The backups:read scope grants permission to list backups without MFA.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Space-separated scopes the client will request. Restricted scopes are rejected. Defaults to data:read_write when omitted.
evidence.answer: On the dynamic registration endpoint, restricted scopes are rejected and data:read_write is the default when no scope is given.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Full access: Read, create, and update your tasks & projects.
evidence.answer: The hosted Todoist MCP server offers full access to read, create, and update tasks and projects.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: endpoint is rate limited per caller.
evidence.answer: The dynamic client registration endpoint is rate limited per caller.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When your application exceeds the maximum token limit or when your application is being suspended due to abuse
evidence.answer: Todoist redirects users with an invalid_application_status error when an app exceeds the maximum token limit or is suspended for abuse.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Limits are applied differently for full and partial syncs.
evidence.answer: API rate limits are applied differently for full syncs and partial syncs; the page gives no numeric limits here.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: You can use our API for free, but depending on your Todoist account plan (or that of the authenticated user), some features may be restricted.
evidence.answer: The Todoist API can be used for free, but some features may be restricted depending on the account plan of the developer or the authenticated user.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Premium limits apply to personal label creation.
evidence.answer: Premium limits apply to personal label creation, and free users who exceed the plan limit receive a premium-only error.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When the user grants your authorization request, the user will be redirected to
evidence.answer: The end user must grant the authorization request; the user is then redirected back to the app's configured redirect URL.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The webhook for a specific user is activated when that user completes the OAuth flow of the app that declares the webhook.
evidence.answer: A webhook for a specific user is activated when that user completes the OAuth flow of the app that declares the webhook.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: To activate webhooks for personal use, you need to complete the OAuth process with your account.
evidence.answer: For personal webhook use, the developer completes the OAuth process with their own account.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If your application has multiple redirect URIs configured, this parameter is required — the request will be rejected with invalid_request if it is omitted.
evidence.answer: If an app has multiple redirect URIs configured, the redirect_uri parameter is required and omitting it is rejected with invalid_request.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
evidence.answer: A redirect URI that is not configured in the App Management Console produces a JSON error to the user's browser.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Array of redirect URIs. Up to 10 entries, each ≤512 characters. Must be HTTPS (localhost is allowed for testing).
evidence.answer: For dynamically registered clients, redirect URIs must be HTTPS (localhost is allowed for testing), up to 10 entries of at most 512 characters each.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Non-empty array of redirect URIs. Must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).
evidence.answer: For Client ID Metadata Document clients, redirect URIs must be a non-empty array and must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The document URL failed SSRF validation (HTTP, private IP, missing path)
evidence.answer: A metadata document URL is rejected if it uses HTTP, a private IP, or lacks a path, among other checks.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: For security reasons, Todoist only allows webhook urls that have HTTPS enabled and no ports specified in the url.
evidence.answer: Todoist only allows webhook URLs that use HTTPS and specify no port.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: A registered Todoist application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret which are needed for the OAuth2 flow.
evidence.answer: Each registered Todoist application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret, which are needed for the OAuth2 flow.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: A comma separated list of permissions that you would like the users to grant to your application.
evidence.answer: The authorization request takes a comma-separated list of scopes that the developer wants users to grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
evidence.answer: Users are redirected to the authorization endpoint at https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token with the following parameters:
evidence.answer: The token exchange is a POST to https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token with the Client ID, Client Secret, and code parameters.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The Client Secret of the Todoist application that you registered.
evidence.answer: The Client Secret is the secret of the registered Todoist application and is used in the token exchange.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Naming: "Todoist" cannot be the primary name of your app.
evidence.answer: The app's name cannot have Todoist as its primary name; use a format such as 'x for Todoist' or 'x with Todoist'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application description must state that it is "not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist."
evidence.answer: The application description must state that it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: you must keep it clearly distinct from Todoist's official products.
evidence.answer: Apps that reference Todoist must keep it clearly distinct from Todoist's official products.

items.reason: Quote states certification isn't required to develop and share the integration with users.
Quote says other users' tokens are obtained via OAuth; no provider review step is mentioned, so the absence claim holds.
Quote says certification is optional and primarily serves to give more visibility.
Quote says passing certification creates a dedicated Integrations Pages listing.
Quote says integrations can be submitted for evaluation and inclusion in the official list, but does not say this follows building an integration in general; it is tied to the certification path.
Quote describes technical review of the demo video, manual testing if necessary, and checking for critical bugs.
Quote states the aim to review submissions and respond within ten business days.
Quote states the aim to get back within two business days.
Quote says meeting the criteria doesn't guarantee passing but is broadly representative.
Quote says the app should complement Todoist and not replicate existing functionality.
Quote says listings are not hosted for solely third-party automation or solely email-forwarding integrations.
Quote says the app exceeding the token limit or being suspended for abuse is affected, but does not mention a redirect or an invalid_application_status error.
Quote states the platform is free to use with any Todoist account.
Quote states the API is free but some features may be restricted by account plan.
Quote says Todoist can help with a Pro account for development; contact with use case and timeline.
Quote states Todoist can't be the primary name of the app.
Quote requires stating the integration is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.
Quote states use of the name or logo follows brand guidelines.
Quote lists marketing description, installation instructions, and website and privacy policy links.
Quote states the icon is JPG on white background at 250x250px.
Quote states JPG screenshots at 1600x1000px, default red theme if Todoist is shown.
Quote states all submission form fields are filled out in English.
Quote states the scope grants read and write access to tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
Quote states the scope grants adding new tasks only and no reading or modifying existing data.
Quotes say certification isn't required to develop and share, and it is optional; no provider review is needed for this setup.
Quotes do not mention App Management Console creation or redirect URL configuration steps, so the ordered gate list cannot be confirmed or refuted.
Quote covers blocking for exceeding the token limit, but also includes suspension for abuse, and the statement's 'limited before approval' framing is not in the quote.
Quotes say passing certification leads to a listing and official list inclusion, implying provider review is needed for the certified listing path.
Quotes describe certification as optional, so the review is not always required for this setup.
Quotes do not list the ordered steps (submit form, submission review, technical review, marketing review); only technical review and submission review timing appear elsewhere.
Technical review covers the demo and bugs, and the submission form asks for descriptions and policy links, but security and data-need checks are not mentioned in the quotes.
Quote states the aim is ten business days for review responses.
Quotes state Todoist cannot be the primary name, the non-affiliation statement is required, and brand guidelines apply.
Quotes support no-certification development and optional certification with about ten business days, but do not mention connecting users in about an hour, so that part is unsupported.
